findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Layer P rationale: rebar Python has legitimate NON-tracker git writes (eval_solver.py / criterion_preview.py disposable fixture repos), so either scope Layer P away from these subtrees, add a distinct sanction category for non-tracker sandbox writes, or drop the 'every raw mutation is seam-internal-or-bypass' claim and account for these sites in the first-scan enumeration.
evidence: Plan: 'rebar's Python writes git ONLY for the tracker or its mirrors, so every raw mutation is either a seam internal (marked once, with reason) or a bypass — no tracker-targeting dataflow analysis needed'

src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:32-33,43-44 — subprocess.run(['git','-C',d,'add','-A']) / commit on a disposable per-eval-case fixture repo (module docstring: 'stands up a disposable, per-case rebar store + fixture repo')
src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py:414-415 — subprocess.run(['git','-C',tmp,'add','-A']) / commit inside a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory detector-preview repo, not the tracker
These are not among the plan's enumerated seam internals and are not bypasses of a store write seam
findings.finding: Layer P's load-bearing rationale ('rebar's Python writes git ONLY for the tracker or its mirrors, so every raw mutation is either a seam internal or a bypass') is factually false: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py and src/rebar/llm/workflow/criterion_preview.py run raw subprocess git add/commit/checkout against disposable, non-tracker sandbox repos (eval fixtures / detector-preview tempdirs). These are legitimate git writes that are neither seam-internal nor bypasses, yet Layer P (module-agnostic, in scope src/rebar/**/*.py) will flag them, forcing spurious '# raw-git-ok' markers that mislabel unrelated code as store-write-seam-internal.
findings.location: Approach — 'Rationale for module-agnostic flagging'; Scope — Layer P scan of src/rebar/**/*.py
scenarios: First full scan flags eval_solver.py and criterion_preview.py as raw-git-write bypasses
Author is forced to annotate non-tracker sandbox git writes with '# raw-git-ok: <reason>', a marker whose stated semantics ('seam-internal') do not fit these sites
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) exclude src/rebar/llm/evals and src/rebar/llm/workflow (or the preview/eval sandbox helpers) from Layer P's scan, or (b) explicitly enumerate eval_solver.py and criterion_preview.py in the first-scan remediation list with a marker reason that names them as disposable non-tracker fixture repos — and revise the Approach rationale to acknowledge non-tracker sandbox git writes rather than asserting rebar Python writes git ONLY for the tracker.

findings.finding: The scope says the lint flags raw git writes 'against the tickets tracker', but the plan never specifies how the scanner distinguishes a tracker-targeting write (add/commit/rm of the store) from a legitimate unrelated git write (e.g. a workflow that commits generated docs, or a script operating on a different repo). Without a stated discriminator the pattern is either over-broad (false positives on every 'git commit') or under-defined.
findings.location: Approach: 'raw git write invocations (add/commit/rm/mv/update-ref against the tickets tracker)'

findings.finding: The plan's seam model and allowlist enumeration ('run_git_write / ticket_txn'; allowlist = 'gitutil.py, lock.py, migration/bootstrap paths') under-identify the real canonical write surface. Multiple live locked-write modules issue RAW `git add`/`git commit`/`reset` on the tracker WITHOUT going through `run_git_write`, and none is named in the plan's allowlist: `_store/event_append.py` (git add/commit via its own raw `_run_git`), `_commands/txn.py::_unstage` (raw `git reset`), and `purge_bridge.py` (raw locked `git add -A`+`commit`). The lint as scoped would fire on these legitimate seam-internal writers.
findings.location: Approach / Scope ('Allowlist file for the legitimate seam internals (gitutil.py, lock.py, migration/bootstrap paths)') and AC 'Tree is clean at landing'

findings.finding: The reconciler is a deliberate SECOND git seam (`_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py` with its own add/commit/update-ref, and `_ref_lock.py` doing update-ref CAS) that writes against the tickets tracker (TICKETS_REF, .tickets-tracker) via `run_git` — not run_git_write. The plan's Scope names only 'gitutil.py, lock.py, migration/bootstrap paths' as allowlist seam internals and does not model the reconciler seam, so the first full scan will flag the entire reconciler write path (and every ref-lock update-ref) as a bypass.
findings.location: Scope ("allowlist file with seam internals … gitutil.py, lock.py, migration/bootstrap paths")

findings.finding: The plan scopes detection to raw git writes 'against the tickets tracker' but gives no mechanism for statically identifying a tracker-targeted write in shell/YAML. The real bypass in reconcile-bridge.yml is `git add -A` + `git commit` that target the tracker ONLY via a preceding `cd .tickets-tracker`; the git line itself carries no tracker token. A substring/regex scan cannot distinguish a tracker commit from an ordinary repo commit without cwd/dataflow tracking the plan never describes.
findings.location: Approach ("scanning … .github/workflows for raw git write invocations … against the tickets tracker")

findings.finding: The plan names `ticket_txn` as one of the two canonical write-seam entry points ('run_git_write / ticket_txn', 'route through run_git_write or extend the seam'), but `ticket_txn` is a stale/relocated symbol: `ticket_txn.py` was moved to `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` (Tier E) and `_engine/ticket_txn.py` is deleted. The teaching error message and AC 'the error message names the seam APIs to use' would name a symbol that no longer exists.
findings.location: Approach / Acceptance Criteria ('route through run_git_write or extend the seam'; 'the error message names the seam APIs to use')
findings.suggested_fix: Name the current seam: `run_git_write` (rebar._store.gitutil) plus the locked-write cores in `rebar._commands.txn` and `rebar._store.event_append`; drop the `ticket_txn` reference.

findings.finding: The plan names `ticket_txn` as a canonical locked write seam (Context, Approach, and the error-message design in Testing), but no current `ticket_txn` seam module exists: it was relocated to `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py`, and the old `_engine/ticket_txn.py` is now only a thin shim. The lint's teaching message and mental model would point authors at a stale name; also `txn.py` itself commits inline (git add+commit inside its critical section rather than exclusively via run_git_write), so it is a seam-INTERNAL that must be allowlisted, not an entrypoint to route through.
findings.location: Context/Problem and Approach ('run_git_write / ticket_txn'); Testing ('route through run_git_write or extend the seam')
findings.suggested_fix: Update Context/Approach/Testing to name `_commands/txn.py` (not `ticket_txn`); add `_commands/txn.py` to the seam-internal allowlist with a reason (holds the lock and commits inline per its docstring), and ensure the teaching message references run_git_write and the txn critical section by their current module paths.

findings.finding: The plan names `run_git_write` as the canonical write seam the lint enforces, but `run_git_write` does NOT take the unified store write lock (I5) — it only self-heals git's index.lock/HEAD-parse faults over `run_git`. The cited bugs (3435, 4dd2) were unlocked WHOLE-INDEX commits (no write lock, no pathspec) and were fixed by routing through the locked, pathspec-scoped `event_append.delete_events` / the write lock — not through `run_git_write`. A `git commit -A` routed through `run_git_write` would PASS this lint yet reproduce the exact I5-violating race that caused those bugs, so the lint's predicate is a proxy that misses the real invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the seam as the write-lock-holding path (ticket_txn / event_append.write_lock / delete_events), and have the lint flag any tracker-targeted add/commit/rm/mv/update-ref that is not inside that locked, pathspec-scoped path — including whole-index (`-a`/`-A`) commits that skip a pathspec.

findings.finding: The repo already has a `# tickets-boundary-ok` in-line marker convention for legitimate tracker-boundary crossings (used across src and scripts). The plan introduces a separate allowlist FILE without reconciling with, or reusing, this existing convention — risking two overlapping opt-out mechanisms for the same concept.
findings.location: Approach / Scope ("Allowlist file for the legitimate seam internals … each entry with a reason comment")
